original_question: For each i, let Gi be the subgroup of GAn(k) that stabilizes k ⊕ kx1 ⊕ ... ⊕ kxi, so that Gn = Aff_n(k), G2 = Aff_2(k) when n = 2, and G1 is the set of triangular automorphisms. Is GAn(k) generated by G1, ..., Gn? If so, is the group described in the source as an amalgamated product of the Gi along pairwise intersections?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 as reformulated group-theoretically in Proposition 1.2, with Theorem 1.3 giving the paper’s stated low-dimensional evidence.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the relevant subgroups G_i as stabilizers of V_i = k ⊕ kx_1 ⊕ ··· ⊕ kx_i inside GA_n(k), correctly notes the special cases G_n = Aff_n(k) and, when n = 2, G_1 is the triangular/Jonquieres subgroup and G_2 = Aff_2(k), and correctly isolates the two issues the paper cares about: generation by the G_i and a generalized amalgamated-product description along pairwise intersections.
missing_details: The paper’s primary formulation is not just the abstract group-theoretic statement; it is phrased first as Conjecture 1.1 about an associated simplicial complex, and Proposition 1.2 gives the equivalent group-theoretic reformulation.
The amalgam in the paper is a generalized amalgamated product of n subgroups along their pairwise intersections, not merely an ordinary two-factor amalgamated product.
The paper separates two assertions: (i) whether GA_n(k) is generated by G_1, ..., G_n, and (ii) whether the subgroup ⟨G_1, ..., G_n⟩ has the generalized amalgamated-product structure.
To be fully stand-alone, the question should define V_i and G_i explicitly as V_i := k ⊕ kx_1 ⊕ ··· ⊕ kx_i and G_i := Stab_{GA_n(k)}(V_i).
The ambient group is GA_n(k) = Aut_k k[x_1, ..., x_n], with k a field and n fixed; this should be stated explicitly.
The paper’s nearby context uses the associated simplicial complex built from cosets/stabilizers of the G_i; that geometric context is implicit in your draft but central to the official formulation.
Theorem 1.3 is not part of the conjectural statement itself; it records the specific verified case emphasized in the introduction and should be kept separate from the conjecture.
refined_question: Let k be a field, let GA_n(k) = Aut_k k[x_1, ..., x_n], and for each 1 ≤ i ≤ n let V_i := k ⊕ kx_1 ⊕ ··· ⊕ kx_i and G_i := {φ ∈ GA_n(k) : φ(V_i) = V_i}. Is GA_n(k) generated by the subgroups G_1, ..., G_n? Moreover, is the subgroup ⟨G_1, ..., G_n⟩ the generalized amalgamated product of the G_i along their pairwise intersections G_i ∩ G_j?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, in the paper’s geometric language, is the simplicial complex naturally attached to the cosets/stabilizers of the subgroups G_1, ..., G_n connected and simply connected?
justification: Your draft is very close to the paper’s intended problem, but it matches most directly the group-theoretic reformulation rather than the paper’s first, official statement. In the introduction, Conjecture 1.1 is given in geometric terms, and Proposition 1.2 translates it into the language of generation by the stabilizer subgroups G_i and generalized amalgamated products. Theorem 1.3 then records the specific low-dimensional case highlighted by the paper. I therefore kept your question narrowly on GA_n(k) and these particular stabilizer subgroups, while separating the generation claim from the stronger amalgam claim and adding the exact definitions needed to make the question stand alone.
